chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the two (Abu Bakr and Umar), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Al-Fazl, do not ask me about them. By Allah, no one from among us has ever died except while being angry with them, and none of us today is except one who is angry with them. The elders among us bequeath this to the young ones. Indeed, they oppressed us regarding our rights and prevented us from our spoils of war (khums). They were the first to ride upon our necks and inflicted upon us a lasting wound in Islam that is never healed, until our Qaim rises or our speaker speaks.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, if our Qaim rises or our speaker speaks, he will reveal from their affairs what was concealed, and conceal from their affairs what was revealed. By Allah, no affliction or matter that runs against us, the People of the Household, has been established except that they two laid its foundation first. Therefore, upon them is the curse of Allah, and the Angels, and all people.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the anger of the Imams towards Abu Bakr and Umar?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the enduring grievance of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the usurpation of their political and financial rights, specifically the khums, by the first two Caliphs. Imam al-Sadiq (as) emphasizes that this initial injustice established the pattern for all subsequent afflictions, promising that the Qaim (Mahdi) will reveal their hidden truths while concealing their apparent piety, thereby validating the eternal curse upon them.
